title.narrative: DRA PCM JR 2024-2026 Sudan

description.narrative: The project aims to provide multi sectorial emergency responses to multiple states affected by war. The project target IDPs and host communities in North, East and South Darfur and Gedaref.
(paid USD103,000)

title.narrative: Adaptations to JR

description.narrative: Adaptations to JR

title.narrative: ACC-I2 - Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries.

description.narrative: As there JR has annual review process ZOA is expecting to make changes in the project 3 times during the project period

comment.narrative: One project adaptation was made in Gedaref and two in South Darfur in response to partner and community feedback. In Gedaref, a ramp was added to the rehabilitated theatre to improve access for persons with disabilities (PWDs), following a recommendation from PTA members. In South Darfur, two activities were revised during the cholera outbreak to redirect resources towards the urgent cholera response.

description.narrative: Capacity strengthening (Education)

title.narrative: EDU-I4 - Number of teachers and other education personnel trained

description.narrative: These activities are all in Darfur and Gedaref: It includes community and stakeholder Mobilization on the importance of Education, formation and training of PTAs, train for education actors and social mobilization for advocacy on education.

comment.narrative: Q2: In South Darfur, ZOA and NAHA conducted three training workshops for 57 Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) members and three workshops for 60 teachers from Nyala North and Nyala South localities. In East Darfur, teachers and other education personnel also received capacity-building training.Q3: In East Darfur, ZOA continued to strengthen the capacity of teachers and education personnel through targeted training and support activities.Q4: In South Darfur, ZOA conducted a three-day training for 15 Ministry of Education directors (13 men and 2 women) from Nyala North and Nyala South localities. In addition, 36 PTA members (25 men and 11 women) and 40 teachers (35 women and 5 men) were trained, enhancing local capacity to support and improve the quality of education services.
Training of teachers and other education personnel and PTA training in Nayal Shamal and Janoub and Ad Du'ayn

Under the ZOA JR5 project in Gedaref, 10 SOS Sahel staff received training on Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL). In partnership with Plan Sudan, ZOA also delivered two workshops on the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) and Localization, reaching 30 participants from the Ministry of Education (MoE), Water and Environmental Sanitation (WES), local authorities, national NGO partners, and five NAHA staff members.

title.narrative: Excreta disposal

description.narrative: Excreta disposal

title.narrative: WSH-I2 - Number of people having access to dignified, safe, clean and functional excreta disposal facilities

description.narrative: ND, ED, SD and GD: Under this output activities are implemented in Darfur and Gedaref it includes: Construction/Rehabilitation of communal latrines in public areas including camps, schools, health centers, market areas, youth centers, etc. In addition, construction of public latrines in Al-Jerafa in Al-mafaza locality of Gadaref state was carried out as part of the Top up (carry over).

comment.narrative: Q1: In Gedaref State, ZOA constructed eight public latrine pits at Al Azaz Sogoura Village Primary School, benefiting approximately 4,000 people.Q4: In South Darfur, ZOA constructed and handed over a six-door VIP latrine with handwashing facilities at Alhumira School in Nyala North. In North Darfur, two public latrines were rehabilitated in the Um-Khibeisha village cluster, Dar El Salam locality.

title.narrative: Formal education

description.narrative: Formal education

title.narrative: EDU-I1 - Number of boys and girls that access safe, quality learning opportunities (formal education)

description.narrative: Under this outupt activities are implemented in both Gedaref and Darfur and it includees the following activities: Distribute essential teaching and learning supplies to students, teachers and education personnel including suporting schools IGA

comment.narrative: In Gedaref, a school unit consisting of two classrooms, one office, and latrines was constructed in Al Jerefat village. In South Darfur, six schools (three in Nyala South and three in Nyala North) received school supplies to support final examinations.
The project continued to target the same beneficiaries and geographic areas as in 2024, with no expansion to new locations or beneficiary groups.

title.narrative: Hygiene promotion (Awareness)

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion (Awareness)

title.narrative: WSH-I6 - Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Under this output, activities are implemented in both Darfur and Gedaref and it includes:Conduct hygiene promotion activities (including home visits, FDG, and training of community hygiene promoters) on market days and using radio messaging to ensure reaching large numbers of people, Conduct Sanitation and Hygiene campaigns to reduce disease outbreaks in high-risk contexts

comment.narrative: Conducted hygiene promotion activities and trained community hygiene promoters in Al Manara IDP Camp in Ad Du'ayn, East Darfur.

Q2: In Gedaref, GPA conducted 21 FGDs and 175 home visits, reaching 700 community members, including persons with disabilities (PWDs). In South Darfur, NAHA trained 20 community hygiene promoters and implemented cholera prevention campaigns through household visits, poster distribution, and mobile loudspeaker announcements.Q4: In South Darfur, ZOA conducted hygiene promotion activities, including home visits, FGDs, and training for 58 hygiene promoters on safe sanitation and cholera prevention, complemented by radio messaging. In North Darfur, two hygiene promotion campaigns and one community training were conducted by 30 hygiene promoters. In Gedaref, GPA carried out home visits promoting hygiene practices, reaching 11,342 individuals.

title.narrative: Hygiene promotion

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion

title.narrative: WSH-I1 - Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Under this output activities are implemented in Darfur and it includes: Distribution and installation of handwashing equipment (including soap) to HHs, schools and health centers and Distribution of hygiene kits.

comment.narrative: Distribution of hygiene kits in An Gabo, East Darfur.

Q1: In South Darfur (Nyala North and South), ZOA conducted a hygiene promotion campaign on safe latrine use, benefiting 440 households, while NAHA’s cholera prevention campaign reached 3,200 people. In Gedaref, GPA distributed hygiene kits to returnees from Gezira through the crisis modifier. In East Darfur, 100 hygiene kits were distributed to internally displaced women in Al Dyaien Rural.Q3: In East Darfur, 90 WASH committee members and 30 community mobilisers were trained on personal hygiene and cholera prevention, and hygiene kits were distributed.Q4: In South Darfur, handwashing stations were installed, WASH NFIs distributed, and latrines desludged as part of the cholera response. In North Darfur, hygiene kits were distributed to 384 households.

title.narrative: Safe and accessible learning environments

description.narrative: Safe and accessible learning environments

title.narrative: EDU-I3 - Number of learning spaces/schools set up or rehabilitated and equipped to meet standards

description.narrative: Under this output 12 schools wll be suported 4 in Gedaref and 8 in Darfur through rehabilitation and/or construction of learning facilities (classrooms, offices, fencing, latrines etc.), construction/upgrading teachers housing, improve school water systems and entertainment facilities. Also, one school (2 class rooms) was contracted in Al-jerafa, in Almaza locality Gedaref as part of the top up from JR4.

comment.narrative: In Gedaref, Al Jerefat village, a school unit (two classrooms and one office) and latrines were constructed. GPA successfully implemented forums on the importance of education at Kassab and Wad Daeef schools. GPA also conducted sessions on social mobilisation, community engagement, and advocacy in Kassab and Wad Zayed villages in Al Gallabat Al Gharbia locality.

Q1: In Gedaref State, ZOA constructed and rehabilitated two schools, improving learning facilities for children.Q2: In South Darfur, NAHA handed over a four-unit latrine block to Salman Alfarisi Elementary School, benefiting approximately 500 female students and 21 female teachers.Q3: In Gedaref State, ZOA continued to strengthen education infrastructure through the construction and rehabilitation of two schools.Q4: In South Darfur, ZOA rehabilitated classrooms, offices, and a library in two schools, provided safe drinking water to Al-Saadia Primary School for Girls, and constructed a VIP latrine at Alsahawa Primary School. In Gedaref State, ZOA constructed and rehabilitated facilities at Kassab Primary School for Girls and Wad Daeef Primary School for Boys, including classrooms and teachers’ offices.

title.narrative: Short-term livelihoods support

description.narrative: Short-term livelihoods support

title.narrative: FSC-I1 - Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihood assets

description.narrative: These activities are planned only in North Darfur and they include the following:Strengthen existing community-based committees (e.g., farmer committees and animal producers, etc.) for improved production (provision of locally procured seeds, tools, potentially business grants), Provision of technical and in-kind support to vulnerable households (women farmers), Construction and supporting committees to operate seed banks, Support Income generating activities (IGAs) targeting vulnerable women, Formation/strengthening and training of VSLA groups, Support animal vaccination campaigns, Training of community animal health workers, providing them with necessary equipment and animal treatments, and Establishment of goat banks (provision of livestock)

comment.narrative: Q4: In North Darfur, one seed bank was constructed and another rehabilitated. In addition, two income-generating activities (IGAs) and 15 goat banks were established. ZOA trained 35 Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs), equipped them with veterinary drugs and equipment, and conducted one livestock treatment campaign.

title.narrative: Water Supply

description.narrative: Water Supply

title.narrative: WSH-I4 - Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Under this output, activities are implemented in both Darfur and Gedaref and it includes: Construction of new/rehabilitation of existing non-functional water points (including hand pumps, boreholes and water yards), Formation and training of Water Resources Management Committees (WRMCs) in target areas for sustained O&M of water points, Support water quality supply chain. In addition, the construction of Al-Jerefat water treatment plant (slow sand filter) and Drilling of Abu Annga water well (27) in Gedaref locality were carried out as part of the top-up (carry over).

comment.narrative: In Al Jerefat village, Gedaref, an elevated water tank and a water distribution point were successfully constructed, and the pipeline connecting the water station to the village was completed.

Q1: In Gedaref, ZOA rehabilitated a water station in Al Kanz village, benefiting 11,500 people. In Gezira State, GPA rehabilitated three water sources and installed solar systems, serving 8,939 IDPs.Q4: In South Darfur, ZOA rehabilitated a mini water station and a water pump station, trained two Water Resources Management Committees, and supported chlorination of 10 water points during the cholera outbreak. In Gedaref, a new borehole was constructed in Abu Al Naja, benefiting 7,948 people, while 10,500 people were reached through water quality monitoring in West Gallabat locality.

title.narrative: Solid waste management
WSH-I5 Number of people living in settlements with a functional solid waste management system

comment.narrative: Q3: In South Darfur, ZOA implemented a clean-up campaign in wadi areas and distributed cleaning tools to IDP gathering centres in Nyala Shamal and Nyala Janoub localities. During the cholera outbreak, ZOA also supported the Ministry of Health (MoH) by covering the rental costs of two trucks used for a large-scale community cleaning campaign.
